translationRepairs: In King Zhao's fourteenth year, Wei Ran recommended Bai Qi to replace Xiang Shou as general and attack Han and Wei, defeating them at Yi Guan, beheading twenty-four thousand, and capturing Wei general Gongsun Xi.

In King Zhao's fourteenth year, Wei Ran recommended Bai Qi to replace Xiang Shou as general and attack Han and Wei, defeating them at Yi Guan, beheading two hundred and forty thousand, and capturing Wei general Gongsun Xi.
斬首二十四萬 is 240,000; literal “twenty-four thousand” undercounts by ten, and “two hundred and forty thousand” matches the Chinese and the idiomatic rendering.
Qin made Marquis of Rang attack Wei, beheaded four thousand, routed Wei general Bao Yuan, obtained Wei three counties.
Qin made Marquis of Rang attack Wei, beheaded forty thousand, routed Wei general Bao Yuan, obtained Wei three counties.
斬首四萬 is 40,000; literal “four thousand” undercounts by ten, and “forty thousand” restores the correct figure.
Next year, Marquis of Rang with Bai Qi guest qing Hu Yang again attacked Zhao Han Wei, broke Mang Mao Hua Yang below, beheaded ten thousand, took Wei Juan, Cai Yang, Chang She, Zhao Guan Jin.
Next year, Marquis of Rang with Bai Qi guest qing Hu Yang again attacked Zhao Han Wei, broke Mang Mao Hua Yang below, beheaded one hundred thousand, took Wei Juan, Cai Yang, Chang She, Zhao Guan Jin.
斬首十萬 is 100,000; literal “ten thousand” undercounts by ten, and “one hundred thousand” matches the Chinese.
In King Zhao's thirty-second year, the Marquis of Rang, serving as chancellor, led troops to attack Wei, routed them at Mang Mao, entered Bei Zhai, and then surrounded Daliang.
In King Zhao's thirty-second year, the Marquis of Rang, serving as chancellor, led troops to attack Wei, routed Mang Mao, entered Bei Zhai, and then surrounded Daliang.
走芒卯 means Qin routed the person Mang Mao; “routed them at Mang Mao” wrongly treats 芒卯 as a place, and “routed Mang Mao” is correct (cf. s0051, s0081).
Qin nibbles away at the Wei clan and exhausts the state of Jin. Though Wei defeated Baozi and ceded eight counties, the land had not yet been fully handed over before Qin's troops came out again.

Qin nibbles away at the Wei clan and exhausts the Jin states. After defeating Baozi and obtaining the cession of eight counties, the land had not yet been fully handed over before Qin's troops came out again.
Continuation from 秦: 戰勝暴子 is Qin’s victory over Baozi, not Wei’s; the proposal removes the reversed victor while preserving the unfinished-cession sequel.
He pulled back Wei's territory north of the Yellow River, taking more than sixty cities, large and small.
He seized Wei's territory north of the Yellow River, taking more than sixty cities, large and small.
拔魏之河內 means he captured/seized Wei’s Henei; “pulled back” misreads 拔, and “seized” is the correct military sense.
The reason Wei and Zhao survive as intact states with vigorous armies and lands not annexed by the feudal lords is that they are able to endure hardship and cede territory generously.
The reason Wey and Zhao survive as intact states with vigorous armies and lands not annexed by the feudal lords is that they are able to endure hardship and treat ceding territory as a grave matter.
重出地 means they treat ceding land as weighty/serious, not that they cede generously; and 衛 is Wey (as in s0043–s0044), distinct from 魏 Wei.
